title: Standup / Sprint Delay — announcement crib
body:
Purpose:
This is a quick crib for the short announcement we need to surface in tomorrow's standups and in the #prod-ops channel about the sprint delay for the rollout of the KV-cache refactor. The goal is to be concise, align managers on tone, and give a compact Q&A so ICs aren't caught off guard in standups.

Audience:
- Primary: engineering teams touching serving-runtime and cache layer (serving-runtime, infra).
- Secondary: SRE, Support, Solutions Eng who may field customer questions.

Desired outcome:
- Team understands scope & expected delay window (not indefinite).
- No spurious escalation; most incidents should be handled as normal SEV triage.
- Managers and on-call know what to say and where the authoritative status lives.

Key message (1-sentence):
"We're pausing the KV-cache refactor rollout for one sprint to address observed edge-case regressions; the team will continue limited verification tests and we expect to resume rollout next sprint — detailed timeline in the ticket."

Slack announcement (short):
[10:00] /prod-ops: Quick update: KV-cache refactor rollout paused for 1 sprint after we observed regressions in prefix caching for mixed-length requests. Expect follow-up on JIRA-OPS-1293 and a short status update in tomorrow's standups. No customer-facing impact currently.

Talking points for standup leads (30–60s):
- One-liner explanation: paused because of regressions surfaced during canary; not a full rollback, we're fixing compatibility tests and adding a small guardrail.
- What this means for my team: no new traffic migrations this sprint; keep working on unit cleanup and the compatibility tests (assignments unchanged).
- If you have a PR that assumes the new cache behavior, flag it and tag @Riya for coordination.
- Where to look for updates: JIRA-OPS-1293 (link), #prod-ops thread pinned.

Manager scripts (for 1:1s or team channels):
- Short, empathetic: "We hit a compatibility hole during canary and we're taking the conservative path to protect product stability. This is expected engineering tradeoff — we'll prioritize the tests that unblock the rollout next sprint."
- Reassurance for delivery: "We believe this will add one sprint of delay to the rollout plan, not the project. If blockers accumulate we'll map scope and share updated delivery.",

Q&A (expected) and suggested responses:
Q: Is this a customer-impacting incident?
A: No current customer impact. Canary traffic flagged regressions early. We paused to fix before wider exposure.

Q: Does this change any SLAs or dedicated/customer commitments?
A: Not today. If that changes we'll escalate to PM/Account teams and open a customer comms thread.

Q: How long is "one sprint"?
A: We mean the current 2-week cycle. We expect to resume rollout at the start of the following sprint, pending verification test results.

Q: Who owns the fix?
A: Eng owners: Mateo (compat tests) and Riya (guardrail + deployment gating). On-call SRE continues to monitor infra metrics as usual.

Open items / notes to self (Sona):
- Confirm that we actually observed the regression across both 16k and 32k sequence canaries (ask Mateo for canary logs). [ACTION: Mateo]
- Add a short test case to the compatibility suite that reproduces the edge-case (priority: high). [ACTION: Riya]
- Draft a customer-facing blurb only if PM requests (don't pre-empt). [ACTION: PM check]

Escalation / when to flip to incident comms:
- Any user-facing errors or increase in 5xx rate linked to cache behavior -> immediate incident channel and page SRE lead.
- If the delay expands beyond two weeks -> escalate to Eng Leadership and GTM for messaging coordination.

Follow-up timeline (proposed):
- Today (EOD): brief Slack message + pin JIRA link.
- Tomorrow standups: 1-sentence readout + refer to lead scripts.
- Mid-sprint (week 1): compatibility test added & initial verification.
- End of sprint: decision point — either resume rollout or extend window with comms.

Quick copy for pin & ticket summary (one line):
Paused KV-cache refactor rollout for one sprint after canary regressions; mitigation: compatibility tests + gating logic; owners: Mateo, Riya; ticket: JIRA-OPS-1293.

Misc scratch ideas (might be useful):
- Could create a tiny synthetic canary that mixes sequence lengths and tenant mix to reproduce locally — faster feedback loop for PRs.
- Consider a temporary metric alert that specifically looks for cache hit-rate divergence between canary and baseline.

Unresolved / questions for leadership:
- Are we okay with adding a short public-facing note if some customers ask? (PM preference)
- If rollout is customer-impacting later, who is primary EM for comms? (nominate placeholder)

Draft checklist before "resume rollout":
- [ ] Compatibility test added and passing in CI.
- [ ] Canary run for mixed-lengths passes N=3.
- [ ] Guardrail in deploy logic to fall back on old cache if error rate spikes.
- [ ] PM sign-off on comms plan if customer impact arises.

Endnotes / links (for people who want to deep dive):
- JIRA-OPS-1293 (main issue)
- Canary run logs: /internal/canaries/kv-refactor/2025-11-14 (ask Mateo)
- Runbook: confluence:ops/quiet-window-runbook

---
Notes to self: keep this short in standups. Don't add technical nuance unless asked. If anyone presses for details, point them to the ticket and say we're fixing tests + adding safeties.

[last edit quick] 2025-11-16 10:12 — trimmed talking points, added checklist and owner assignments.
